findings.affected_requirement: BMad AC-3; spec.md FR-014; contracts/exact-resolution-service.md negative-outcome matrix
findings.evidence: The resolver throws InvalidDataException when the eligible consumer or provider count is not exactly one and on normalization mismatch. The coordinator converts those documented eligible-negative outcomes to generic Refused and never calls the persistence store. The accepted-negative-matrix integration test explicitly asserts Refused, zero store calls, and an empty Uncertainties table for variable_target, disallowed_invocation, malformed_provider, provider_out_of_root, unmatched, normalization_mismatch, and multiple_providers. The authority requires zero Edge plus one bounded idempotent warning or Uncertainty carrying repository-relative evidence.
findings.correction_outcome: Generate safe owner-anchored Uncertainty decisions for every eligible non-exact reason, persist them idempotently with repository-relative evidence and no Edge, and replace the negative integration assertions with assertions for the required persisted diagnostic outcome.

findings.affected_requirement: BMad AC-3 and AC-7; spec.md FR-014 and FR-022; contracts/resolution-persistence-and-retrieval.md authorization-aware diagnostic retrieval
findings.evidence: Reviewed unsupported observations are deliberately stored as targetless unknown_target Uncertainty records. KnowledgeStoreRepository correctly asks the production authorization verifier to recheck only the owner Repository when TargetRepositoryId is null, but RepositoryAuthorizationVerifier rejects every required-repository set whose count is not exactly two. Consequently an authorized owner cannot retrieve the durable unsupported diagnostic. Existing authorization tests use fixture scopes or target-bearing records and do not exercise the production verifier's one-Repository case.
findings.correction_outcome: Make the production verifier validate any bounded non-empty distinct required-Repository set, including the owner-only targetless Uncertainty case, while preserving fail-closed authorization. Add production-verifier retrieval tests for authorized and unauthorized targetless records.

findings.affected_requirement: spec.md FR-017 and SC-006; contracts/git-revision-acquisition.md operation-local cleanup ownership
findings.evidence: The coordinator disposes leases sequentially in a finally loop without isolating disposal failures. A lease DisposeAsync throws when best-effort cleanup remains incomplete; that exception stops iteration, so later acquired snapshots are not disposed and the caller loses the remaining lease references. This creates a bounded-disk and private-worktree leakage path precisely when cleanup is degraded, and no coordinator test covers multiple leases with one throwing disposer.
findings.correction_outcome: Attempt disposal of every acquired lease even when one cleanup fails, retain or aggregate only sanitized bounded cleanup failure information, and add a coordinator regression test proving one failing disposer cannot prevent cleanup of the other snapshot leases.
